page: Microsoft Azure M64ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64). Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with dedicated CPU allocation, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of memory. This hardware allocation yields a substantial memory density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server does not include any GPU accelerators.

The instance does not feature local ephemeral disk storage, requiring external storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for operating system and application data volumes. In terms of network provisioning, the configuration includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating integration with virtual networks or externally attached public IP addresses for external connectivity.

From an architectural perspective, M64ps_v4 combines high-density memory with the power and compute efficiency of ARM64 processors. Because local disk performance is entirely reliant on attached remote volumes, I/O profiles depend on configured storage tiers. This profile is engineered specifically for large in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, and enterprise data processing applications that require extensive memory footprints on ARM-supported environments.
description: Microsoft Azure M64ps_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64) running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high density of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included. Local ephemeral disk storage is not present, making the instance dependent on remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for all filesystem requirements. Networking configurations include zero default complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its large memory footprint on an energy-efficient ARM processor foundation, the instance offers significant memory capacity per compute unit. It is suited for memory-intensive enterprise software, large-scale in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, and memory-constrained analytical data processing workloads compiled for ARM64 platforms.
